name: API Version Enumeration (Improper Inventory Management)
description: Probe old API versions (v0, v1, v2, beta, legacy) that developers forgot to retire. OWASP API9 – Improper Inventory Management. Old versions often lack the security controls of current versions — missing auth checks, exposing deleted records, or returning more data than intended.
notes: APIs commonly expose /api/v0/, /api/v1/, /api/v2/, /api/beta/, /api/legacy/. Old versions may not require authentication, may expose soft-deleted records, or may have weaker authorization. Swagger UI (usually at /swagger, /api-docs, /openapi.json) often documents ALL versions including deprecated ones — check it first to map the full surface. Also try /api/v0/admin/, /internal/, /debug/ endpoints.

variations.command: for ver in v0 v1 v2 v3 beta legacy internal; do echo "=== $ver ==="; curl -s http://<target>/api/$ver/<endpoint> -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token>" | jq; done
variations.caption: Probe multiple version prefixes in a loop
variations.label: Batch loop

variations.caption: Access soft-deleted records via old API version
variations.label: GET request

variations.caption: Dump all API paths from Swagger spec to discover old/hidden endpoints
variations.label: Swagger/OpenAPI

variations.caption: OpenAPI spec — alternative path for endpoint discovery
variations.label: Swagger/OpenAPI

variations.caption: Fuzz API version and prefix with ffuf
variations.label: ffuf brute

examples.command:
curl -s http://<target>/api/v0/supplier-companies/deleted -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token>" | jq
curl -s http://<target>/api/v0/customers/deleted | jq
examples.caption: CWES M18: v0 endpoint returns deleted records with no auth — data exposure via deprecated version

references.title: OWASP API Security Top 10 – API9:2023 Improper Inventory Management

recommended.note: Test old version endpoints for BOLA — may lack authorization checks entirely
Credential attacks if old version auth endpoint is exposed

defense.why_it_works: API versioning (v1, v2, beta, legacy) allows developers to maintain backward compatibility while adding security controls to newer versions. Old API versions are often left running but not maintained — they may lack authentication requirements, input validation, or rate-limiting added to current versions. OWASP API9 (Improper Inventory Management) describes scenarios where retired or shadow API endpoints expose data and functionality that the current version no longer permits.
defense.prerequisites: Any network access to the API host. Knowledge (or guessing) of common version prefixes: /api/v0/, /api/v1/, /api/v2/, /api/beta/, /api/legacy/, /v1/, /v2/. ffuf or gobuster for systematic enumeration. No authentication required for the enumeration phase itself if old versions lack auth.
defense.impact: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application + T1087 Account Discovery. Access to unprotected legacy endpoints that bypass current auth controls. Exposure of data the current API hides (e.g., full PII in v1 vs. masked in v2). Exploit vulnerabilities patched in current version but present in legacy version. Shadow APIs not in API documentation may expose internal admin functions.
defense.detection:
API gateway access logs showing requests to deprecated version path prefixes (/v0/, /beta/, /legacy/). Alert on traffic to API paths that are not in the current API specification (use OpenAPI spec as allowlist). Monitor for version-scanning patterns: sequential requests to /api/v1/, /api/v2/, /api/v3/ from same source. WAF virtual patching on retired API paths — return 404 even if the route is still active, log the attempt.
Abnormal request patterns to public endpoint → elevated 4xx/5xx or unusual methods/paths → server process (w3wp.exe/service) spawns shell/LOLbins or loads non-standard modules → optional outbound callback (DET0080/AN0219).
Suspicious requests in access logs → spike of 5xx or WAF blocks → web server interpreter (apache2/nginx/php-fpm/node/python) spawns /bin/sh, curl, wget, socat, or writes webshell → outbound callback (AN0220).
Containerized app: suspicious request in ingress/app logs → container process spawns shell/exec → egress to Internet or metadata service 169.254.169.254 (AN0222).
ALB/ELB/Cloud LB logs show exploit-like inputs or error spikes → workload spawns shell or reaches metadata API → egress to new external hosts (AN0223).
defense.artifacts: API gateway logs: GET /api/v0/* or /api/beta/* requests | WAF alert: access to deprecated API version paths | Application logs: requests to deprecated route handlers | Network capture: systematic version path enumeration from single source
defense.prevention: Maintain a complete API inventory (OpenAPI/Swagger) and decommission unused versions by removing the route handlers, not just hiding them. Use an API gateway to enforce an allowlist of active API paths — requests to unlisted paths return 404. Require authentication on all API versions equally. Apply the same rate-limiting, WAF rules, and security controls to all API versions, including beta. Regularly audit deployed API routes against the official inventory. Use api-version deprecation sunset headers to signal clients before removal.
defense.evasion: Try non-obvious version strings: /api/internal/, /api/admin/, /api/debug/, /api/test/, /api/dev/. Fuzz with HTTP header versioning (Accept: application/vnd.api+json;version=2) instead of URL versioning. Access via different hostnames if APIs are served on multiple domains (api.internal vs api.example.com).
defense.misconfiguration: Legacy API versions left active in routing configuration but removed from documentation and security review. No API gateway allowlist enforcing active-only routes. Beta/test API routes deployed to production without authentication. Different security middleware applied to v1 vs v2 routes — v1 lacks auth requirement. No automated inventory audit against deployed routes.
defense.secure_config:
# Express — only active version mounted, gateway enforces allowlist:
// Remove all unused router registrations:
app.use('/api/v2', authenticate, rateLimiter, router_v2)
// v1 completely removed — no route handler, no 404 → 410 Gone:
app.use('/api/v1', (req, res) => res.status(410).json({ error: 'API v1 retired. Use /api/v2' }))
app.use('/api/beta', (req, res) => res.status(410).json({ error: 'Beta API retired.' }))

# API Gateway (Kong) — path allowlist:
# services:
#   - name: api-v2-only
#     url: http://backend:3000/api/v2
#     routes:
#       - paths: [/api/v2/]  # only v2 exposed through gateway

# OpenAPI spec as source of truth — CI check:
# 1. Extract all routes from deployed app
# 2. Compare against openapi.yaml paths
# 3. Fail build if unlisted routes found
